analysis.title: Weekly Market Guide
key_insights: The S&P 500 has moved sideways since early August against high oil prices and high interest rates. About 46% of S&P 1500 stocks are more than 20% below their highs.
Large-cap Technology and Energy, plus defensive rotation into Health Care and Consumer Staples, have held the index near its highs. Economic- and interest-sensitive areas have come under pressure.

The US 10-year Treasury yield has driven market rotations through 2026. With yields consolidating over the past couple of weeks, the average stock is bouncing and breaking above resistance as it nears prior highs.

Oil is a key influence on interest rates because it affects inflation and potential Fed actions. If commodity prices stall or fall from elevated levels, the impetus for Fed hikes could fade, easing rates and supporting market breadth.

The market is increasingly split between AI-levered stocks and the rest. Tech is up big on days when most other areas are down, and the reverse. About 20% of the S&P 500 (about 100 stocks) have a negative 1-year beta.
The split reflects Tech concentration and investors rotating within equities rather than selling outright. The note says this raises the importance of diversification.
Nominal GDP growth of 6.3% is above the 5.1% 10-year Treasury yield, which the note says supports fundamental strength. Elevated rates are partly driven by growth buoyed by the capex boom.
Investment-grade credit remains healthy and spreads are narrow. High-yield and other higher-levered credit shows some deterioration.
The note recommends dialing back exposure to High-Beta Momentum areas and boosting Quality in portfolios.
High oil prices and bond yields weigh on valuation multiples. Without strong fundamentals from the AI/capex boom, equities would probably be under more pressure.

The earnings backdrop is strong with continued upward revisions, and the note expects equities to extend their uptrend over the next 12 months. Q3 earnings season is the key catalyst in the coming weeks, with early reads positive.
